# Questions to answer while presenting

**Why does DRHQ need a DQN if G acts?** DQN learns off-policy from transitions generated by G and exploration. Its flexible value approximation supplies the preferred action. G handles inspectable action selection.

**What updates after an interaction?** The transition enters replay. A sampled minibatch trains Q with a TD target and Huber loss. Two separate minibatches train G. The target network copies Q every 100 updates in the local implementation.

**Why cross-entropy?** DRHQ's one-hot best-action target trains the probability of selecting that action. DRSQ instead uses the whole soft preference distribution. DRQ attempts numerical value fitting.

**Why is G monotonic?** Positive clearance and powers between one and two leave the derivative sign determined by the signed coefficient at a fixed checkpoint. The claim concerns nonnegative continuous traffic inputs, conditional on the clearance flag. A new checkpoint can change coefficient signs.

**How does your code differ from the paper?** Two through groups, synthetic FIFO queues, 32 inputs, 56 actor parameters, weights outside powers, simpler teacher architecture, different timing and hyperparameters. There are no turning vehicles, physical spillback, pedestrians or sensor noise. The paper's observed UDOT demand, SUMO environment and 352-parameter controller are reviewed separately.

**How did you obtain the result?** Run 4 algorithms with 3 training seeds for 50 episodes each. Freeze the models. Evaluate 2 scenarios with 10 disjoint arrival streams across 15 controllers per stream: 3 baselines and 12 learned checkpoints. Read the metric from raw CSVs and compute the ratio against local Actuated.

**Is the comparison fair?** Every controller sees the same pre-generated arrivals for its demand seed. No model is picked by test performance. Baselines use their usual restricted observations. Learned policies have an idealized approach detector. The pairing reduces demand-stream confounding but does not make this synthetic environment realistic.

**What does the confidence interval mean?** Resample ten paired held-out demand streams after averaging the three trained checkpoints. It measures demand variation conditional on these models. It does not fully quantify training uncertainty. Inspect training_seed_summary.csv separately.

**Why retain DRQ?** Failure is part of the comparison. Restricted scores can fit action values poorly, leaving severe queues. Those rows remain in the summary and CSVs even when their scale would flatten the other plotted bars.

**Could your metric hide unfinished cars?** It includes their accumulated waiting inside the horizon. It excludes future waiting after the horizon. Completed-only statistics alone could hide them, so report pending vehicles and throughput alongside delay.

**What do the extra cases establish?** Empty traffic has zero delay, bursts and reversal exercise decisions, and overload deliberately creates residual queues. All sixteen diagnostic rollouts conserve vehicles, produce finite values and leave model parameters unchanged. They are diagnostic checks, not exhaustive road-safety validation.

**What exactly did each person do?** State a real task, show the relevant cell or file, describe its check and result, and link their own run or commit. The supplied proposed division is not a completed contribution record.
